mockups.title: Ember Spit — molten charcoal
mockups.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit / stylized-concept.
Asset type: a full-resolution game VFX concept mockup, not an implemented gameplay screenshot.
Input image 1 is the edit target: an actual 1920x1080 Caves of Ooo GameView. Keep the EXACT camera angle, zoom, 16:9 framing, composition, terrain geometry, town layout, actor positions and actor sizes. Preserve the right HUD, bottom hotbar, text, black fog boundaries and background lighting. Do not crop, zoom, pan, enlarge characters, add an inset, or redraw the town in a different style.
Change only the small existing cyan spell effect between the teal player near pixel (746,315) and the olive recipient near (852,315), replacing it with the spell described below. Retain the existing low-poly carved/toylike 3D visual language and match the current ground projection.
The request is for DRAMATICALLY MORE READABLE effects at this unchanged gameplay zoom: a bold luminous primary shape roughly 150–200 pixels across, bright milky highlights, a darker saturated edge that separates it from the olive ground, and 100–180 densely packed, closely spaced glowing particles with varied size and overlapping short motion streaks. Airborne ribbons and particles may extend decoratively beyond a cell; keep the contact rooted at the real recipient/path. Use restrained local light spill and a soft colored halo, never a washed-out full-screen flash. The effect should be immediately noticeable in the entire zoomed-out screenshot, not only in a detail crop. Preserve readable faces, the teal player silhouette through clear openings in the effect.
Output one full 16:9 image with the same complete viewport. No contact sheet, inset, comparison split, new labels or watermark.
Spell concept: FIRE / EMBER SPIT. Replace the cyan water shards with a powerful compact charcoal comet fired from the teal player's outstretched hand toward the olive recipient. A hot ivory-yellow molten core, saturated amber and coral-orange carved wood-grain flame ribbons, a thick tapering luminous trail, and a broad upward-curling impact crown make the release readable. Use charcoal-violet undersides to keep solid 3D facets visible. Scatter many gold sparks, coral ember flakes and a few dark coal chips with bright edges around the trail and contact. The main crown rises to two character heights while leaving the recipient's face exposed through its center. This is a fiery projectile and impact with local airborne overhang; do not set the town or extra actors on fire. Fire hue must be very bright and vivid against this unchanged green scene.
Density refinement from the user: substantially REDUCE SPACE BETWEEN PARTICLES. Pack the main spell envelope into a cohesive connected luminous volume: overlapping particles and short streaks close the gaps along streams and arcs, with densely layered small motes surrounding the larger pieces. Avoid a dotted line of isolated fragments or a sparse scattering. Keep a dense bright center and a rich contiguous particle mantle, graduating to a thinner outer edge; character visibility comes from deliberate openings around faces, not from making the overall effect sparse.
